suitability_reason: Alimony deductibility of $15,000 attorney-fee payments turns on §71(b)(1)(D) (liability surviving payee's death), read from the instrument's 'paid in full' language; a rule-based test on instrument terms.

taxpayer.notes: Divorcing in California; January 30, 2017 Superior Court order for temporary spousal support and $15,000 toward ex-spouse's attorney fees.

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Argues the $15,000 attorney-fee payments are temporary spousal support terminating on death, hence deductible alimony.
conceded: Petitioner conceded $4,097 of the claimed alimony deduction is not deductible
Respondent conceded petitioner is entitled to a partial deduction of $7,520
Respondent conceded the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: January 30, 2017 California Superior Court order: $9,146 monthly alimony; temporary spousal support continues until death of either party
findings_of_fact.snippet: Under section 2 of t he order, “temporary spousal support pursuant to this order shall continue until the death of either party.”

findings_of_fact.fact: Section 7 of the order: petitioner to pay $15,000 toward ex-spouse's attorney's fees, $2,500 monthly from March 1, 2017 until paid in full, to ex-spouse's attorney
findings_of_fact.snippet: in monthly installments of $2,500, commencing March 1, 2017, and every month after until paid in full.

findings_of_fact.fact: Return prepared with CPA claimed $135,516 alimony deduction; respondent allowed $108,898.70, disallowing $26,617.30
findings_of_fact.snippet: respondent allowed $108,8 98.70 of petitioner’s claim ed alimony deduction, resulting in a disallowance of $26,617.30.

findings_of_fact.fact: Parties agree §71(b)(1)(A), (B), (C) are satisfied; dispute only (D)
findings_of_fact.snippet: satisfy the requirements of section 71(b) (1)(A), (B), and (C).

findings_of_fact.fact: Court concludes liability for $15,000 attorney fees would survive ex-spouse's death
findings_of_fact.snippet: We conclude that petitioner ’s liability to pay his ex -spouse’s attorney’s fees of $ 15,000 would survive he r death.

issues.question: Is the $15,000 payment to the ex-spouse's attorney deductible alimony under sections 71(b) and 215 for 2017?
issues.holding: No; obligation to pay until 'paid in full' survives the payee's death, failing §71(b)(1)(D); $15,000 deduction denied.
issues.computable_reason: Given instrument terms (no termination on payee death), §71(b)(1)(D) fails mechanically.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: $15,000 attorney-fee alimony deduction denied; $7,520 allowed per respondent concession; no 6662(a) penalty (conceded).

notes: Some facts stipulated. Disallowed $26,617 = $4,097 (petitioner concession) + $7,520 (respondent concession) + $15,000 (disputed) per fn 2. Pre-TCJA instrument; §§71/215 repeal not applicable. Court relied on Johanson (9th Cir.) and prior Tax Court cases (Logue, Stedman).
